newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Placer Dome to appeal environmental charges.
newsitem.headline: Placer Dome to appeal environmental charges.

text.p: Canadian mining company Placer Dome Inc said on Friday it will appeal before Costa Rican courts the government's suspension of its gold mining activities in the north of the country.
The Vancouver, B.C.-based company said in a statement it had requested a legal hold on the government order before Costa Rica's Supreme Court.
Last week the government ordered the company to partially suspend gold exploration on charges it was damaging the environment, harming the countryside and disturbing local wildlife.
But the company again denied the charges that it harmed the Cerro Crucitas site and said the government's Environment Ministry did not follow correct procedures in ordering the suspension.
Placer Dome began operations in Costa Rica, near its border with Nicaragua, in 1993 on about 2,000 hectares (5,000 acres) granted in a government concession.
The government has given Placer Dome a period of three moonths to reduce and repair environmental damage caused. The company has also been ordered to pay 56 million colones ($250,000) within 15 days.
Placer Dome has invested about $20 million in the Cerro Crucitas project and so far identified a resource of 2.2 million ounces of gold, a company spokesman has said.
